question: Haunted by gender
answer:
Several of the Club's jokes took aim at the spiritualist movement, a movement not incidentally dominated by women whose participants often sympathized with the women’s suffrage movement. 

The Club sarcastically lamented in 1883 that they had “sought in vain for a haunted house, in which to enjoy at least one of our dinners. Evidently ghosts refuse to affiliate with us, though an invitation to meet such on earth will at any future time be eagerly accepted and promptly acted upon.” This offer to dine with a ghost if one could be found mocked those who believed in ghosts, as the Club men made clear that in the absence of evidence of any such spirits in existence “on earth” their raison d'etre remained. Indeed, while beliefs in "fortune telling and spiritualism" continued "to play upon the weaker side of effete or sickly humanity, there will exist a necessity for just such a bold, brave body of men as compose the Thirteen Club" opined one member.
